FN-1198PL3-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 173
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/10/2026
Senate Bill 173 as introduced, beginning October 1, 2026, would provide circuit and district
courts, with exclusive and concurrent jurisdiction over violations of domestic violence
protection orders, which could decrease the obligations of municipal courts and increase the
obligations of circuit and district courts by undetermined amounts dependent upon any increase
in the number of new cases and cases transferred to district and circuit courts from other courts
pursuant to this bill.
Page 1

FN-1198PL3-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 173
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: «Released Date»
Senate Bill 173 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary, beginning October 1, 2026, would
provide district courts with exclusive jurisdiction, over violations of domestic violence
protection orders, except for violations under the jurisdiction of juvenile courts. This could
decrease the obligations of municipal courts and increase the obligations of district courts by
undetermined amounts dependent upon any increase in the number of new cases and cases
transferred to district courts from other courts pursuant to this bill.
Page 1

FN-1198PL3-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 173
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/24/2026
Senate Bill 173 as passed the Senate, beginning October 1, 2026, would provide district courts
with exclusive jurisdiction over violations of domestic violence protection orders, except for
violations under the jurisdiction of juvenile courts, which could decrease the obligations of
municipal courts and increase the obligations of district courts by undetermined amounts,
respectively, dependent upon the number of cases heard in district courts that otherwise would
be heard in other courts due to the provisions of this bill.
Page 1

FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 173
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Senator Lance Bell
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 02/25/2026
Senate Bill 173 as reported by the Committee on Judiciary, beginning October 1, 2026, would
provide district courts with exclusive jurisdiction over violations of domestic violence
protection orders, with exceptions, which could decrease the obligations of municipal courts and
increase the obligations of district courts by undetermined amounts, respectively, dependent
upon the number of cases heard in district courts that otherwise would be heard in other courts
due to the provisions of this bill.
